summary: Bursting mini-workloads causing slot fragmentation and eviction loop in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (MaplePay, dedicated) reports repeated throughput collapse and cascading evictions in their reserved GPU pool during short-lived, high-concurrency microbursts.

Impact:
- MaplesPay sees p99 generation latency increase from ~120ms to >3s for ~20% of requests during midday window (11:20-11:50 UTC).
- Several long-running jobs evicted transiently, causing client errors and retry storms.
- Billing spike risk due to repeated slot allocation/eviction churn.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: reserved-pool-12 (12x A10G), region us-east-1, pinned model: redwood-open-7b@v2.1.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive scale-down after 30s of idle slots, background prefetch enabled, KV cache warm retention=300s.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a flood of short (5-50 token) concurrent streams from many client connections over 2-3 minute windows (simulate bursting mini-workloads).
2) Observe allocator behaviour: many small batches created, slot fragmenting across GPUs.
3) After burst stops, autoscaler rapidly shrinks capacity, but some ephemeral prefetch/checkpointer threads hold GPU page mappings and cause eviction-reschedule loops.

Observed behavior:
- Continuous short-lived allocation and eviction loops (worker logs show repeated attach/detach).
- Autoscaler not provisioning capacity quickly enough for bursty pattern because bursts are below the autoscale stabilization threshold.
- KV cache growth on a subset of tenants prevents clean slot reclamation, leaving many "half-occupied" slots with prefetch leases.
- P99 latency spikes correlated with high OOM/eviction counts in node-exporter metrics and increased NVLink retry counters.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should add capacity for sustained bursts or let burst-aware policy open temporary burst slots without triggering eviction loops.
- Prefetch/checkpointer should release GPU resources promptly on preemption to avoid slot fragmentation.

Logs / Metrics / Evidence:
- Grafana dashboard snapshots: generation_p99 spike @ 2026-03-10T11:23:12Z (link: https://grafana.redwood/invite/abc123).
- Node exporter: eviction_count increased by 87 between 11:20-11:25 UTC on pool nodes.
- Allocator logs: repeated messages: "slot-attached pid=9837 prefetch-lease=held" followed by "gpu-evict-requeue pid=9837".
- Customer provided request-id samples: [req-ff12, req-ff13, req-ff18] showing 502s on retries.
- Slack thread: #support-mapplepay (https://slack.redwood/archives/C09ABC/xyz789).

Investigation so far:
- Reproduced burst pattern in staging with synthetic short-stream load; observed same slot fragmentation and delayed slot reclaim.
- Heuristic: autoscaler uses 30s idle window; bursts often last ~45-120s with high fanout but low per-stream duration, so scale decisions oscillate.
- Identified two contributing code paths: (1) prefetch/checkpointer holds page mappings preventing immediate eviction; (2) allocator returns partially filled slots back into pool causing fragmentation rather than coalescing.
- Temporary experiment: increased autoscale min-capacity for the pool avoided immediate collapse in staging, but is not acceptable as default.

Workarounds / Mitigation:
- For MaplePay: applied a per-customer autoscale override to increase min-replicas by 2 for the peak window (11:00-12:00 UTC) — mitigated P99 spikes for the remainder of the window.
- Recommend customer implement client-side jittered backoff to avoid synchronized reconnects.

Action items / Next steps:
1) Engineering to add burst-aware autoscale mode that recognizes high-concurrency short-lived streams and provisions transient burst slots without triggering aggressive scale-down. (Owner: Infra-Alloc team)
2) Modify prefetch/checkpointer to release page mappings on preemption faster (Owner: Serving Runtime).
3) Investigate allocator coalescing to avoid half-occupied slot fragmentation (Owner: Scheduler).
4) Add targeted alerting: detect eviction-requeue loops and auto-escalate to on-call.
5) Follow up with MaplePay CS to monitor during next peak window and validate remediation.

Reference runbooks and related tickets: SUP-334567, SUP-41258.
